findings.title: Providers with equal order() are picked arbitrarily, silently bypassing the old single-provider guard
findings.body: The old code threw when more than one CryptoProvider was on the classpath. The new code sorts by order() and takes the first element. DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200 in this PR, so a tie is possible. Ties are then resolved by ServiceLoader/classpath order, which is not a defined contract. If a FIPS deployment has both the FIPS and the default (or elytron) provider jar on the classpath, the non-FIPS provider can be selected with no error. The only trace is a debug log line. The removed guard existed to prevent exactly this. Equal top-order providers should still fail fast, or the FIPS provider should be given a strictly higher order.

findings.title: AuthzClient.create() installs a process-wide, one-shot crypto provider visible only to its own classloader
findings.body: CryptoIntegration.init() is global and idempotent: it only runs detection while cryptoProvider is null, and later calls are no-ops. Here it is called with AuthzClient.class.getClassLoader(), so only providers visible from that loader are considered. If the real provider (Default, Elytron or FIPS) is only visible through another classloader, or is initialized later with a different loader, the AuthzClientCryptoProvider stub becomes the provider for the whole JVM and stays there. Every later crypto call then fails with UnsupportedOperationException. Before this PR, authz-client did not touch global crypto state at all. Consider not initializing global state from client construction, or only doing so when no provider has been set.

findings.title: Most CryptoProvider methods are placeholder stubs throwing 'Not supported yet.'
findings.body: getAlgorithmProvider, getCertificateUtils, getPemUtils, getOCSPProver, getIdentityExtractorProvider, createECParams, getKeyPairGen, getKeyFactory, getAesCbcCipher, getAesGcmCipher, getSecretKeyFact, getX509CertFactory, getCertStore, getCertPathBuilder, getSignature, wrapFactoryForTruststore and ECDSACryptoProvider.getPublicFromPrivate all throw UnsupportedOperationException("Not supported yet."). This provider is registered through the service file and is selected whenever it is the only provider present. Any code path that reaches one of these methods then fails with a message that names nothing useful. The class Javadoc ("Simple crypto provider to be used with the authz-client") does not mention these gaps. Document the supported operations, and make each unsupported operation name itself in the exception, or remove stubs that cannot be reached.

findings.title: getBouncyCastleProvider() returns the provider of a default KeyStore, not a BouncyCastle provider
findings.body: The method creates a KeyStore of the default type and returns its provider (typically a JDK SUN/SunJSSE provider). The method name and the CryptoProvider contract say it returns the BouncyCastle provider. Callers that use it for Signature, Cipher or other lookups will silently get a non-BC provider, which may lack the required algorithms. A new KeyStore object is also allocated on every call just to read its provider. Return the real BC provider, or throw UnsupportedOperationException like the other unsupported methods in this class.

findings.title: New abstract order() method on the public CryptoProvider SPI breaks existing implementations
findings.body: order() is added as an abstract interface method with no default. Any CryptoProvider implementation outside the three in-repo providers, including third-party or downstream ones, will stop compiling. If it is compiled against an older interface, it fails at runtime with AbstractMethodError when order() is called during provider sorting. A default implementation would keep existing providers loading, while the in-repo providers keep their explicit overrides.

findings.title: ECDSA conversion test is only a self round-trip, and uses a P-256 key for ES384/ES512
findings.body: The test asserts asn1derToConcatenatedRS(concatenatedRSToASN1DER(x)) == x. It checks the two conversions only against each other, so a shared encoding mistake (wrong DER SEQUENCE or INTEGER layout, for example) passes unnoticed. The produced DER is never checked with the JDK's Signature.verify. The key is also always generated as P-256 (KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC")), so the ES384 and ES512 cases run with 32-byte R/S values padded to 48 and 66 bytes, not the real curve sizes. Verify each DER signature with the JDK verifier, and use P-384 and P-521 keys for ES384 and ES512. The 33-byte leading-zero INTEGER case should also be covered deterministically.

findings.title: integerToBytes silently truncates over-long DER integers instead of rejecting them
findings.body: When the decoded INTEGER has more bytes than the field length (qLength < bytes.length), the code keeps only the trailing bytes and discards the high-order ones. A malformed or non-canonical DER integer, for example r with an extra leading 0x01 byte, is turned into a different, valid-looking concatenated signature instead of an IOException. Verification then depends on the JDK rejecting the altered value. The conversion should check that the value fits in qLength bytes, allowing only a single leading zero.

findings.title: Indefinite-length marker reaches new byte[-1] and throws an unchecked exception
findings.body: readLength() returns -1 for the indefinite-length marker 0x80. readInteger() passes that value straight to read(), where new byte[length] throws NegativeArraySizeException. The decoder's contract reports malformed DER through IOException, which the callers declare, so malformed input to asn1derToConcatenatedRS escapes as a RuntimeException. readNext() has the same problem. readLength should reject negative lengths with an IOException.

findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder statements in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.body: Lines 114-115 build two ASN1Encoder instances, encode rBigInteger and sBigInteger, and discard the results. The returned DER comes only from the writeDerSeq call below. The dead statements suggest the values feed into the output when they do not, and they should be removed.
